- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.30), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect market resilience or mean reversion.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +0.70 sentiment) by forecasting higher prices for 1–3 days; apply lagged correction: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0 unit after spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend + negative sentiment, model may underestimate; add 0.3–0.7 to forecast to capture rebound.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum; if sentiment turns positive mid-horizon, adjust forecast upward by 0.2–0.5 units in final 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., +0.70 then -0.40), model may misalign with sentiment cycle; align forecast to sentiment’s recent direction, not just average.
